entities.summary:
The Chinese Communist Party (CCP), founded in Shanghai in 1921, is the world's largest political party with over 95 million members and has ruled the People's Republic of China since 1949. Under the CCP's leadership, China transformed from one of the world's poorest countries to the second-largest economy, lifting 800 million people out of poverty in the fastest reduction of mass poverty in human history.

The CCP was founded with Soviet Comintern assistance in 1921 by Chen Duxiu and Li Dazhao, but Mao Zedong emerged as its dominant leader during the Long March (1934-35). The CCP-KMT Civil War ended in 1949 when Mao declared the People's Republic of China. Mao's Great Leap Forward (1958-1962) caused 30-45 million famine deaths, and the Cultural Revolution (1966-1976) killed hundreds of thousands and destroyed much of China's cultural heritage.

Deng Xiaoping's post-1978 'reform and opening up' policies created state-directed capitalism that grew China's economy from $150 billion (1978) to $18 trillion (2023). Xi Jinping's consolidation of power since 2012 — removing presidential term limits, absorbing Hong Kong's autonomy, and pursuing Chinese hegemony — has made the CCP's authoritarian capitalism the most significant geopolitical challenge to liberal democracy since the Cold War. China's 'Belt and Road Initiative' extending infrastructure investment across 140+ countries represents the CCP's most ambitious foreign policy program.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Chinese Communist Party's 75-year rule transformed the world's most populous nation from poverty to the second-largest economy, combining economic miracle with political authoritarianism in the defining governance model of the 21st century.
